find: At the 48+ target, merge parts per material, prune shadow casters and add LOD or instancing (STATUS:84); 5,843 draw calls at 48 is the known wall.
text: At the 48+ target, cut the per-soldier draw calls, prune shadow casters and add LOD or instancing (STATUS:84); 5,843 draw calls at 48 is the known wall. Baseline (headless eval with tools/preview.js on the booted game, counting each soldier's group): a styled bot is 122-140 meshes, that is 66-77 primitive parts plus 56-64 ink hulls (the player 154), and after stylizeScene every part has its own toon material (distinct materials = parts; core:404). Every buildEntity part casts a shadow (core:686). The steps-1-6 report:94 counted 105 meshes and 49 outlines on 2026-10-16. The legacy code has no SkinnedMesh, InstancedMesh, BatchedMesh or LOD (grep over the three engine files: 0 hits). The parts animate independently, so the static merge (mergeStaticGroup, core:360-387, which bakes each part's transform into one geometry) cannot apply. Merging per material needs rigid skinning (one bone per part) or BatchedMesh with a transform per part; a spike measures draw calls and GPU time for each option at 48 soldiers on real hardware.

find: Avoid compiling one program per faction variant: v2 can pass palette colours as uniforms or instance attributes.
text: In r128 a material colour is a uniform, so the faction recolour by itself adds no shader program (applyFaction core:643-653 and buildEntity core:657-669 set only .color); what made 16 programs against 9 is not established (a spike can count programs per material parameter set). In v2, palette colours passed as uniforms or instance attributes keep one material for every faction, which also allows instancing.
